newsitem.title: GERMANY: Much DM repo trade still in London - German traders.
newsitem.headline: Much DM repo trade still in London - German traders.

text.p: Leading German money market traders said on Tuesday that the bulk of mark repo business was still taking place in London despite the Bundesbank's decision to scrap the minimum reserve requirement on such trades.
Bernd Franke, a department director at Dresdner Bank in Frankfurt, said he expected Germany to handle at most 40 percent of mark repo business, with the other 60 percent bring handled in London.
"Before the minimum reserve requirement was dropped Frankfurt had a share of no more than 25 percent," he said.

Detlef Bindert of Deutsche Bank said that although German banks had repatriated most of their mark repo business to Germany since the reserve requirement changes, this was not necessarily the case for foreign banks even though there was now no competitive benefit to handling such business abroad.
Many foreign institutes did a large part of their capital market trading in London and therefore also sought refinancing via the money market in the City.
Repo business allows a borrower to borrow funds against a deposit of securities.
